newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's CPI up 0.2 percent m/m in February.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's CPI up 0.2 percent m/m in February.

text.p: Tunisia's consumer price index (CPI) rose by 0.2 percent in February compared to its level in January, official statistics showed on Wednesday.
It was up 0.6 percent in January-February 1997 compared to its level in December 1996.
The average increase of consumer prices during the first two months of the year is put at 3.4 percent compared to 5.2 percent during the corresponding period of 1996.
In February, prices rose by 0.4 percent for food, by 0.1 percent for housing, by 0.1 percent for health care, by 0.5 percent for clothes, by 0.1 percent for leisures, and 0.0 percent for transports.
Inflation as measured by the CPI was 3.7 percent for the whole year 1996 from 6.3 percent in 1995.
The cut in the inflation rate for 1996 was made possible by the decrease of prices of foodstuffs thanks rainfalls which led to higher agriculture output after a two-year drought.
CPI is forecast to rise by 4.2 percent in 1997.
